newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June spot natgas prices ease on futures slump.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June spot natgas prices ease on futures slump.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for June 1 fell off previous highs on Thursday as futures faltered and cool weather continued in the East and Midwest, industry sources said.

June Louisiana Gulf Coast prices slipped about five cents to the mid-to-high $2.20s, with Transco (Station 65) quoted mostly at $2.28-2.30. These prices indicate a gain of about 15-20 cents from May indices.
Prompting physical gas to soften was the decline of NYMEX's July Henry Hub contract to a low of $2.24, down 7.6 cents from Wednesday's session.
For Friday delivery, Gulf prices were also lower in the low-to-mid $2.20s.
In south Texas, June prices were quoted at $2.17-2.20, up 15 cents from May 1 amid temperature highs in Houston in the high-80s.
In the Midwest, where temperatures remain below normal, June 1 prices softened a few cents to about $2.10, indicating a jump of about 15 cents from May index levels.
Temperatures in Chicago were forecast to reach highs in the low-to-mid 60s Friday and Saturday, Weather Services Corp said.
In the East, New York city gate prices for June 1 were quoted at $2.48-2.53.

In the West, Permian prices began as high as $2.12 but then softened to about $2.06-2.07 by late morning. Southern California border prices covered a wide range of $2.14 to $2.26, with the lower-priced deals surfacing in late morning trade.

The 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit, shut late Monday for repairs, is expected to restart late Thursday, while Texas Utilities' 1,150 MW Comanche Peak 2 unit was increasing power earlier today and expected to reach full power later today.
Meanwhile, Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit is expected to restart this weekend following its refueling outage.
